Question B-003-021-010.

Why the correct answer is right: Mounting high-gain antennas above nearby structures helps keep the main RF beam from being directed at people inside them.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "So they will not direct RF energy toward people in nearby structures": This is the correct choice because mounting high-gain antennas above nearby structures helps keep the main RF beam from being directed at people inside them.
- sourceIndex 1: "So static electricity buildup is minimized": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from So they will not direct RF energy toward people in nearby structures. In RF exposure controls for UHF, microwave, handheld, indoor, dipole, and high-gain antennas, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 2: "So they will not damage nearby structures with RF energy": This answer would fit a different fault than So they will not direct RF energy toward people in nearby structures. In RF exposure controls for UHF, microwave, handheld, indoor, dipole, and high-gain antennas, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "So they will receive more sky waves and fewer ground waves": This option confuses another station topic with So they will not direct RF energy toward people in nearby structures. In RF exposure controls for UHF, microwave, handheld, indoor, dipole, and high-gain antennas, grounding words can sound plausible, but this choice puts the ground connection in the wrong role for this question.
